standard_prerequisites.name: The free system on three generators
standard_prerequisites.statement: F_3 is freely generated by three elements a_1, a_2, a_3.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the starting point of the construction.

standard_prerequisites.name: The iterated union
standard_prerequisites.statement: N_omega is the union of a countable chain of copies of the free system, each elementary in the next.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the system shown to be unconfined but not free.

standard_prerequisites.name: Freely generated systems
standard_prerequisites.statement: A system is free when it is freely generated by some set, in particular it is generated by that set.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what the constructed system fails to be.

core_obligations: Start from the free system on three generators and an element built from the generators as in the cited example (source line 1099).
Form the countable union of a chain of unconfined systems and observe that unconfinedness is detected on a finite subset, so the union is unconfined (source line 1100).
Show that the union is not finitely generated and conclude that it is not free (source lines 1100-1101).

proof_roadmap.step: Build the chain and take its union.
Unconfinedness transfers to the union; finite generation fails, so it is not free.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled proposition at source lines 1097-1098: there exists a countable unconfined Steiner triple system which is not free. The author gave it no label, so its position is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 1099-1102) constructs the witness as the union of a countable elementary chain of unconfined systems, then uses two facts that the statement does not mention: unconfinedness is a property of finite subsets, so it survives the union, while finite generation does not survive, which is what makes the union fail to be free. The statement records only the existence of such a system.
